assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the retired printer's flat press PDF of the Harborline weekly listing sheet (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered into a live merge template downstream).

Document: single sheet, US LETTER PORTRAIT (215.9 x 279.4 mm / 8.5 x 11 in), one record, fonts fully embedded as subsets, media box = trim (no separate bleed box present; a with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called). Produced from a real page-layout document so convert_pdf_to_indd returns clean, editable frames.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (the apparent blocks, top to bottom):
- ADDRESS line, top, one line, small-caps humanist sans, Sea Slate.
- HEADLINE, transitional serif, large, Deep Harbour Navy.
- One large HERO PHOTOGRAPH, reading as a wide letterbox band across the sheet.
- A three-line DESCRIPTION, transitional serif, Deep Harbour Navy.
- A BEDS / BATHS / SQ FT strip, humanist sans, Sea Slate, separated by hairline Weathered Rope Tan rules.
- The PRICE, transitional serif, large, Deep Harbour Navy, a thin Buoy Red rule beneath.
- The AGENT line, humanist sans, small, Sea Slate.
- A small REFERENCE CODE line, humanist sans, very small, Sea Slate, at the foot.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering traps):
- The DESCRIPTION, the BEDS/BATHS/SQ FT strip, the PRICE and the small REFERENCE CODE are ONE continuous text story in a SINGLE text frame flowing top to bottom (run order: DESCRIPTION, then the strip, then PRICE, then the REFERENCE CODE line). The ADDRESS line and the AGENT line each sit in their own standalone frame.
- generate_indd_mapping_prompt's convenience readout (textContent) SILENTLY OMITS the fourteen-character REFERENCE-CODE run (e.g. 'REF HL-25-0148') while KEEPING its trailing line break, so the reference-code placeholder is simply absent from the readout (mappings silently missing) and every character offset computed past that point is short by exactly that run's length -- yet the validator still returns VALID. The true story must be rebuilt from the exported IDML by unzipping it and concatenating the frame's content runs, never trusted from the readout.
- The DESCRIPTION sub-run lives in a FIXED-MEASURE region sized for the short 2025-book entries (roughly three lines at 10.5/13.5 pt, no auto-grow). A longer string does NOT spill and does NOT error: it oversets and simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so a merged page comes back looking finished with the copy ending mid-sentence at trim. There is no overset readout anywhere in the chain.
- The HERO frame reads as a wide letterbox in this printed sample, but its REAL bounds are close to SQUARE (approx 1 : 1.04). Its content fitting is a CENTRE-ANCHORED PROPORTIONAL FILL exposed in NO readout -- not in the conversion result, the mapping readout, the validator, or the merge response -- so any image bound into it is re-cropped from its own centre regardless of how it was prepared, and a house composed high in its own frame loses its roofline off the top.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): ADDRESS | HEADLINE | DESCRIPTION | BEDS | BATHS | SQFT | PRICE | AGENT | REF_CODE | plus one HERO graphic frame (the picture well).

Colours: Cream #F4ECDD ground, Deep Harbour Navy #12324A headline / description / price, Weathered Rope Tan #B48A54 hairline rules, Sea Slate #5C6E74 address / strip / agent / reference code, Buoy Red #A6392E thin rule under the price. Embedded faces: 'Harborline Text' (transitional serif -- headline, description, price) and 'Coastline Sans' (humanist sans -- address, strip, agent, reference code). No Adobe Fonts face can reach this merged sheet; it inherits only these embedded subsets.

assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph of the front window of a small harbour-front real-estate office, shot slightly from the side with the harbour and moored boats reflected in the glass. Painted on the glass in CREAM paint is the office's house mark, occupying only about the central third of the frame: a circular ROPE RING enclosing a simple LIGHTHOUSE, with the letters H and R below the lighthouse. The rope ring is rendered as a fine repeating twist of short cream strokes with HAIRLINE GAPS between the twists, and the R carries a small enclosed counter (the little hole in the bowl of the letter). Uneven daylight so the RIGHT SIDE of the mark falls into soft shadow where the thin cream paint runs close in value to a pale reflection in the glass. Realistic window framing, faint fingerprints and reflections, casual real-world snapshot, not a studio shot; the fine rope gaps and the small R counter are delicate enough that they would close up if the mark were reproduced small.

assets.content:
HARBORLINE REALTY -- a note from Dana on how we want to look (for the designer)

WHO WE ARE
Eight of us, one office on the harbour, since 2009. I run it. We list the whole mid coast book -- a three hundred and twenty thousand dollar corner-lot starter one week and a four and a half million place out on the point the next -- and both matter to us the same. We are grounded, coastal, understated. We describe the house, not ourselves, and we never oversell.

THE TWO OTHER SIGNS IN TOWN
One is a national franchise storefront: loud, red, everything shouting, the same template whether it is a cottage or a compound. The other is a discount flat-fee outfit that makes every listing look like a classified ad. We do not want to be either. When I say a sheet looks cheap I mean this: too much on the page, the price screaming, a photo that fights the type, blacks gone grey, a logo that is nearly ours but not.

THE TWO REGISTERS (this is the whole job)
The point estate at four and a half million sells to people over fifty with cash who read restraint as proof we can be trusted with the sale: one photograph, deep margins, quiet type, the price set small and sure. The corner-lot starter at three-twenty sells to first-timers under thirty-five who need the price, the bed count and the open-house time to reach them from across a room: brighter, denser, price forward. Style the whole book like the estate and the starters look empty and evasive; style it like the starter and the estate looks like volume work in front of a vendor paying a six-figure commission. Make the difference read -- but both still have to be obviously us.

THE MARK
The rope ring around a lighthouse with the H and the R is our mark. It is painted on the office window and that glass is the only place it still exists; the artwork was lost years ago. Whatever goes on the posts has to be that mark, recovered, knuckle for knuckle. Not something close to it, not redrawn into a font.

THE OPEN HOUSE POSTS
Prices move on Thursdays. Whatever you hand us for the open houses I have to be able to open and change a price in myself, in a minute, without paying anyone twice.

THE ROSTER
We should be carrying eleven active this week. The Sea Meadow cottage on Beauchamp went under agreement Thursday -- it should be off the run, but Monday's export may still have it in. If anything else looks off, ask me: two sheets went out last month with January's prices and I am not doing that again.

-- Dana Marlow
